plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate leveraged ETF exposure. Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate. conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration, but still carries market exposure. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim SOXL and SPAL to reduce leveraged exposure and meet the mandate. Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and comply with the mandate. Trim QQQI to 15% to rebalance the portfolio for a broader mix. Buy XOM at 4% and ZS at 3% as quality scanner setups to diversify and add growth.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for ~2.5%/month growth with a risk-first approach. It reduces leverage and concentration while blending broad index and quality tech. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a balanced growth potential.

plan: Add to SOXL and SPAL to increase leveraged exposure, staying within the mandate. Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate. Add to CRWD, pressing on a strong performer. Buy TSM at 7% and NBIS at 5% as high-scoring scanner setups to lean into growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month growth by stretching exposure and using leverage. It significantly increases both upside and drawdown potential, with leveraged ETFs subject to decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage the higher risk of substantial losses.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure. Sell CRWD to reduce high-beta single name exposure. Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% to prioritize income and monthly distributions. Trim SPY to 20% and QQQ to 10% to rebalance for an income focus and meet the mandate.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, prioritizing steady monthly distributions and low drawdown. It rotates into income ETFs and broad index, cutting high-beta names. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in selloffs, so this is not a savings account.
